questions.problem:
If $v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]$ is an eigenvector of 
$A=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 \\ 6 & 7\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =8,$
then what is the value of $\frac{b}{a}?$
questions.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =8.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 \\ 6 & 7\end{aligned}]-8[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-12 & 2 \\ 6 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}-12{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0 \\ 6{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-12 & 2 & 0 \\ 6 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-12 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
-12{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=\frac{1}{6}{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{6}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=-12,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -12\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{b}{a}=\frac{-12}{-2}=6.$

(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.

questions.problem:
Given that $\lambda =2$ and $\lambda =-1$ are the eigenvalues of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ 5 & -3\end{aligned}]$,
find two linearly independent eigenvectors of $A.$
questions.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

With that in mind, let's consider each of the eigenvalues separately. 

- For $\lambda =2,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ 5 & -3\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 5 & -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0 \\ 5{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 0 \\ 5 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{5}{2}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

- For $\lambda =-1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ 5 & -3\end{aligned}]-(-1)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0 \\ 5{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 0 \\ 5 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=\frac{2}{5}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{5}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=5,$ we get the eigenvector
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, two linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix $A$ are

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$

$$

questions.problem:
Given that $\lambda =-3$ and $\lambda =4$ are the eigenvalues of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 5 & -1\end{aligned}]$,
find two linearly independent eigenvectors of $A.$
questions.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

With that in mind, let's consider each of the eigenvalues separately. 

- For $\lambda =-3,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 5 & -1\end{aligned}]-(-3)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ 5 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0 \\ 5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & 0 \\ 5 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain  ${x}_{1}=-\frac{2}{5}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{2}{5}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=5,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$

- For $\lambda =4,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 5 & -1\end{aligned}]-4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ 5 & -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0 \\ 5{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to its row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 0 \\ 5 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{5}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=-3,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -3\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, two linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix $A$ are

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

$$

$$
{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=0 \\ -12{x}_{1}+18{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=2,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

- For $\lambda =29,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}11 & -6 \\ -12 & 25\end{aligned}]-29[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-18 & -6 \\ -12 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{\begin{aligned}-18{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=0 \\ -12{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-18 & -6 & 0 \\ -12 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{2}{3}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-18 & -6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable.

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.

${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$

$$

$$

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.

$$

$$

$$
{\begin{aligned}-6{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 6 & 0 \\ 3 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-6 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}

that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\,\lambda=1$, then what is the value of $\,\dfrac{b}{a}\,?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A - \lambda I) \textbf{x}=\mathbf{0}.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =1.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 \\ -1 & -4\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ -1 & -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=0 \\ -{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 0 \\ -1 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). So, $x_2$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
x_1+5x_2=0
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
x_1=-5x_2.
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069178/assets/f8c4aba8e8fb922f08741deb8df0fe4f47c64c29b647fec7da2b0ce1b4367225.png)

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069178/assets/5f7d229b6636bbfbe8eab4bdb7a6b8e72bb21c9cc9e66b1b4d607fd0e5e352e0.png)

Finally, $\dfrac{b}{a}=\dfrac{-1}{5}=-\dfrac{1}{5}.$
